source: Stay alive above all else: get to air when drowning, run and eat when hurt, hold a weapon when something hostile is close, and sleep through the night in a bed.
Never let hunger become an emergency. Eat well before the hunger bar starts draining health, and go looking for food while there is still time to find it.
Keep a home base: gather wood, craft and place a room of chests, remember where it is, and use it to store surplus food, ore and building blocks.

Stay out of water you cannot see the bottom of. Getting to air when drowning is already a rule; this is the half that stops it happening -- only enter shallow, open water, never enclosed or underground water, and never swim far from shore.
Do not fight without a weapon in hand, and do not go back to where you last died until it is daylight and you are armed.

Run from what you cannot fight. Strays and the illager family shoot and charge from further away than you notice them, so put real distance between you and them rather than backing off a few blocks. Standing still is never the answer to a mob: mobs do not wander off because you waited, so never answer a mob by staying put.

Cold is a way to die here, not just weather. If you start freezing, that is a countdown: get out of the snow and under cover, or put something warm between you and it. Standing where you are does not warm you up.
Never walk off a drop of four blocks or more. Go around, or dig a staircase down -- falling is a way to die that nothing else in this policy can save you from.

Never approach a hostile mob, and never chase one. Nothing worth having is standing next to a zombie: the mobs come to you, so closing distance only ever buys damage, and doing it unarmed is how this bot has died most often. This goes double for what the goal loop does between rules -- searching for an entity, walking back to a death spot for dropped gear, or looting near a spawner is approaching, whatever it is called. Endermen are the sharpest case: neutral until looked at or struck, lethal after, and they follow you when they teleport.

A bed is the cheapest night there is: sleeping through the dark costs nothing and skips every shelter rule, so getting one is worth a detour long before it is urgent. It is three wool and three planks here, nothing exotic -- hunt sheep for the wool, craft it, and put it down somewhere sheltered. Do not spend an LLM turn asking how.
Keep out of the water rather than only climbing out of it. Wading is how this bot freezes, loses its path halfway across, and drowns; the shore is always the better route even when it is longer.

Be armed before you need to be. Crafting a weapon and drawing it are both free, and going into the dark without one is what most of this bot's deaths have had in common -- eleven of seventeen in one soak.

Never go back to where you died until it is daylight and you are holding a weapon. Whatever killed you is still there, your gear is next to it, and the bot has died five times at one spot in a single game-day doing exactly this.

A bed is only worth having where it is safe to sleep. Do not place one within reach of something hunting, and do not cross a killing field to reach one -- digging in for the night is better than a bed you die in.

When the pathfinder keeps failing from the same block, stop asking it. The route is not there; go somewhere else and try from a different place. Retrying in position is how whole game-days disappear into a single hole.
goal: Stay alive indefinitely and make yourself harder to kill: keep a home base with a bed and stocked chests, and keep food, shelter and a weapon between you and every way this world can end you. If the land within your search radius has no food to gather or hunt, your base is in the wrong place: relocate it to a biome that can feed you, and move your bed and stores there.

rules.name: surface_when_drowning
rules.description: Out of air is the one emergency that beats everything else.

rules.name: keep_out_of_water
rules.description: Stay out of the water in the first place. surface_when_drowning is the rescue; this is the part the bot kept writing for itself, because its own memory has said 'avoid water' since the first session and nothing in the profile ever acted on it. Wading also means freezing in a snowy biome and pathing that gives up halfway across. Interrupts on purpose: a bot that only avoids water while idle avoids nothing, because the wading happens mid-path. It drowned on 2026-08-09 doing exactly that. The is_idle gate came off with it: interrupt priority and an is_idle trigger cancel out, which is how the first pass at this audit left eight rules exactly as starved as before.

rules.name: give_up_on_a_stuck_path
rules.description: Forty failed pathfinds in a row without moving a block means the route is not happening from here, and the forty-first will not be the one. Walking somewhere else is the only thing that changes the answer. Measured: 6281 pathfinds burned on one block in a single game-day, and another grind to 1106 visited nodes at one block immediately before the agent dropped off the server.

rules.name: surface_when_night_finds_you_underground
rules.description: Interrupts on purpose, and pinned: climb_out_of_the_deep only reaches below y=45, but soak 12 died over and over between y=55 and y=80 -- caving at night, where the arrows and the creepers are. Andy worked this out before the policy did and wrote it into its own self layer twice: "if it is night and I am underground, immediately go to the surface and stay there until morning". The is_sheltered exemption keeps a dug-in foxhole from being dragged out of its own roof.

rules.name: climb_out_of_the_deep
rules.description: Interrupts on purpose, and pinned: depth is not something to fix when convenient, and the first merge of this rule quietly rewrote it to idle. Nothing in this policy could see how deep the bot was. The goal loop writes its own mining code, and in the first forty minutes of soak 12 that code took it to y=20, y=19 and y=-7 -- three lives, each one a creeper or a fall, each followed by a respawn at camp and a hundred-and-fifty-block walk straight back down to the corpse. The death-spot rules cannot help: they only trigger once it has already arrived, and two of those deaths were armed, which is the one case leave_your_death_spot ignores. A bot whose best weapon is a wooden sword has no business below the ore line, so the depth itself is the trigger.

rules.name: flee_when_hurt
rules.description: Get clear and eat back the health lost. Gated on actually having food: fleeing and failing to eat does not raise health, so without this it re-fires every cooldown and cancels every other action forever.

rules.name: hold_weapon_when_threatened
rules.description: Something hostile is close, you own a weapon, and it is not in your hand. All three clauses earn their place: without "not holding" every fire after the first is a no-op that still cancels whatever was running, and without "has_item weapon" the rule fires forever at an empty inventory with nothing it could possibly equip -- observed live, every few seconds, for an hour. Do not write this as "has_item sword": sword is not a family name and matches nothing.

rules.name: arm_yourself_before_dark
rules.description: Draw the weapon at dusk rather than when something is already shooting. hold_weapon_when_threatened waits for a hostile within 12, which in a soak meant the bot met its first arrow with an axe in the bag and a log in its hand. Free, and it stops as soon as the weapon is out.

rules.name: flee_ranged_raiders
rules.description: Everything that kills this agent from outside cowardice's radius, in one rule, with the list taken from counting actual deaths rather than from what sounds dangerous. Stray, chillager and the illager family were the first; Illusioner, Iceologer, the mutant skeleton and two kinds of creeper earned their places later. Every id was checked against the server with `summon` before being added, because a name the client spells differently matches nothing and fails silently -- see tools/live_test.sh raider. Zombie is the biggest killer by far and is deliberately absent: it is melee, which is cowardice's job, and this rule is pinned and interrupts everything, so it must not fire for things fleeing cannot fix. Gated on not being under cover: a capped foxhole beats a footrace, and climbing out of one to flee is how the footrace starts. Skeleton earned its place the same way the others did. After the flee comes a dig_in: distance alone leaves the bot standing in the open for the next volley, and the agent kept teaching itself exactly this flee-then-burrow pattern until it was folded in here.

rules.name: dig_in_when_hunted
rules.description: Something hostile closing and no roof: put ground between you and it, day or night, armed or not. Was night-or-unarmed only, and the agent kept writing itself a pinned always-shelter rule (46 fires in 20 minutes, no sheltered gate, digging deeper each time) because armed daytime chases had no answer but the cowardice footrace. The stay holds until the area is quiet AND it is not night, so a daytime dig does not pop back out while the mob is still pacing overhead; once capped there is no clear path to the bot, so cowardice and self_defense stand down on their own.

rules.name: back_off_from_endermen
rules.description: Endermen are the one mob where approaching is the whole mistake: they are neutral until looked at or hit, and then they teleport with you and out-damage anything wooden. Get distance and wait it out rather than fighting or chasing. Folded from a self rule the bot wrote after being hit by one -- its version also fired on health_below 90, which is true nearly always, so it retreated from nothing eleven times an hour.

rules.name: dig_in_out_of_the_cold
rules.description: Freezing and no roof: a capped foxhole is out of the snowfall, which is what freezing means here -- and it is free, where the prompt version below costs a turn per firing and was the single biggest prompt bill on stormy nights. Digging down also exits powder snow. The prompt survives it, gated on not-sheltered, for the cold the hole cannot fix.

rules.name: get_out_of_the_cold
rules.description: The freeze meter is filling and there is about two seconds before it starts taking health. Andy has died "froze to death" here. This is a prompt rather than named actions because the fix genuinely depends on what is around -- dig into a hillside, get off the ice, put a roof and a light overhead, or craft leather -- and there is no single action that is right in all of them. What is certainly wrong is waiting, which is what the agent wrote for itself every time, having no is_freezing to compile against.

do.message:
YOU ARE FREEZING. The freeze meter is nearly full and it will start taking your health, then kill you -- you have died this way before. This is not something to wait out; standing still is what fills the meter.
Do one of these NOW, whichever is closest:
- If you are standing in powder snow, get OUT of it first -- !moveAway 8. It looks like a normal snow block and it is the fastest way to freeze.
- Get under cover and out of the weather: dig two blocks into the nearest hillside, or dig down two and put a block over your head. Being enclosed stops the snow reaching you.
- Put a heat source next to you: !placeHere torch, or a campfire if you have one. Then stay beside it, not merely near it.
- Leather armour stops freezing entirely. If you have leather, !craftRecipe leather_boots and the rest, and !equip them.
If none of that is possible where you stand, walk out of the snow: pick a direction and !moveAway 32, then look again. Any of these beats another second in the open.

rules.name: dig_in_at_your_death_spot
rules.description: Your respawn point is where you died, so at night the reflex to walk away is a walk through whatever killed you. Measured: 28 deaths in one game-day, every one of them at -53,88,-66, which was both the bed and an exposed cliff -- leave_your_death_spot fired, set out on its 24-block walk unarmed in the dark, and lost the bot again before it arrived, doubling its own backoff each time until it stopped mattering. Ground goes over your head where you stand, in the two seconds you reliably have, and you wait for morning. Daylight is leave_your_death_spot's job.

rules.name: leave_your_death_spot
rules.description: Whatever killed you is probably still standing there and your gear is on the ground next to it, so walking back in unarmed is how you die twice. This was previously inexpressible: the compiler wanted it, had no condition for "where I died", and wrote at_position 0,0,0 -- a placeholder matching only the world origin, so the rule never fired once. Gated on not holding a weapon, because armed and in daylight is exactly when going back to collect your things is the right call. Night was folded in here once and it made things worse -- the walk is what killed the bot, 28 times in one game-day -- so dig_in_at_your_death_spot owns the dark now and this rule owns the daylight.

rules.name: sleep_at_night
rules.description: Head for a bed at dusk and stay put until morning -- but break off if something hostile closes in, instead of standing still while it hits you. Not while something is hunting nearby -- a bed is only worth the walk if the walk is survivable; if it is not, dig_in_for_the_night is the better night.

rules.name: dig_in_for_the_night
rules.description: Night with no bed and no roof: foxhole up and wait for dawn, for free -- and do it even mid-task. Interrupts everything on purpose: the agent kept writing itself pinned shelter-beats-the-job rules every rough night until this was promoted to match. The is_sheltered gate keeps it silent while building indoors, so only surface wandering gets interrupted. The prompt version below only exists for the nights the dig fails -- lava underfoot, undiggable ground -- which its no-progress backoff surfaces on its own.

rules.name: wait_out_the_night_under_cover
rules.description: Already under a roof at night with no bed: hold position until dawn. Free, and it keeps the goal loop parked -- an idle sheltered bot would otherwise resume self-prompting and wander back out into the dark.

rules.name: shelter_when_night_and_no_bed
rules.description: Nightfall with no bed anywhere. Without this the bot stands in the open until something kills it. But the old wording -- 'seal the hole, leaving no opening a mob can path through' -- is what made it entomb itself: its own memory records building 3x3 shelters around itself repeatedly and then being unable to travel, which is the 'every attempt to travel failed' loop that burned a whole session. A shelter you cannot leave is a grave. Long cooldown on purpose: a prompt does not change the world, so re-issuing it every minute only cancels the digging it asked for.

do.message:
It is night and you have no bed, so you cannot sleep through it -- you have to survive it instead. Do NOT stand in the open. Dig two blocks into the nearest hillside, or straight down two, and cover the opening above you with dirt, cobblestone or planks. Place a torch inside so nothing spawns in with you.
READ THIS PART CAREFULLY, YOU HAVE GOT IT WRONG BEFORE. You have repeatedly walled yourself in on all sides and then been unable to travel at all for the rest of the night and the whole next day. Do not build a box around yourself. You need exactly enough cover to stop a mob reaching you and NOT ONE BLOCK MORE:
- Cover yourself with blocks YOU CAN BREAK -- dirt, planks, cobblestone. Never seal yourself behind anything you have no tool for.
- Do not place blocks on all four sides plus the roof. A two-deep hole with the entrance covered is enough.
- Before you settle, know which single block you will break to get out, and make sure it is one you can reach and break from where you are standing.
AT FIRST LIGHT, LEAVE. Break your way out and get back to work -- do not sit in the hole through the day. If you ever find that you cannot travel anywhere, the first thing to suspect is that you are still inside one of these shelters: break out sideways at your own feet level before trying to go anywhere.

rules.name: keep_a_crafting_table_at_camp
rules.description: Every craft above a 2x2 grid needs a table, and the bot has been building a throwaway one per craft: soak 11 shows "Crafted 1 crafting_table / Placed / Collected 0 crafting_table" over and over, four planks burned each time because the pickup after the break keeps failing. Worse, when the planks run short the table cannot be built at all and the craft dies with "needs a crafting table and none was found within 16 blocks" -- which is exactly how build_a_furnace failed on its first two fires. One standing table where the bot lives fixes both. If a table is already in the bag the craft step is a no-op and the place step still puts it down.

rules.name: craft_a_weapon
rules.description: Unarmed with wood in the bag. craftRecipe already crafts the planks and sticks on the way, so this needs no reasoning -- and the LLM turn it replaced was the difference between having a sword at dusk and not. Interrupts on purpose: being unarmed is what most of this bot's deaths have in common, and an idle-gated craft never got a turn to fix it. The is_idle gate came off after a soak: eleven of seventeen deaths were unarmed and this fired twice in six game-days, because interrupt priority means nothing while the trigger still waits for an idle that does not come.

rules.name: craft_a_pickaxe
rules.description: Wood in the bag and no pickaxe. On this modded server bare hands cannot clear stone inside dig_in's time budget, so every foxhole attempt over stone failed and fell through to the paid prompt -- a wooden pickaxe is the difference between shelter being free and shelter costing an LLM turn. It also makes cobblestone drop, which is cap material and a furnace. craftRecipe crafts the planks and sticks on the way. Interrupts on purpose: one shot, in place, and everything downstream is blocked without it. The is_idle gate came off with it: interrupt priority and an is_idle trigger cancel out, which is how the first pass at this audit left eight rules exactly as starved as before.

rules.name: craft_shovel_for_snow
rules.description: Snow underfoot and nothing to dig it with. A named craft; there was never a decision here. It still needs the wood the craft consumes: without that guard this fired twenty times in six hours on an agent that owned no planks, and every one of them ended in "You do not have the resources to craft a wooden_shovel". craft_a_weapon already carries the same guard. Interrupts on purpose: one shot and in place. The is_idle gate came off with it: interrupt priority and an is_idle trigger cancel out, which is how the first pass at this audit left eight rules exactly as starved as before.

rules.name: weave_wool_from_string
rules.description: The bed chain has never once completed, and the reason is not the policy: hunt_sheep_for_wool fired fifteen times in soak 12 and answered "Could not find any sheep in 48 blocks" twenty-four times. There are no sheep in this taiga. Four string is a wool, spiders drop string, and the hunting mode kills spiders already -- so this is the wool source that exists here. A bed is worth more than any other item in this policy: it skips the night entirely, and seventeen of soak 12's twenty-three deaths were at night.

rules.name: steer_clear_of_lava
rules.description: First lava death in twelve soaks, at (-243,93,223), and there was no rule against it because there had never been a reason for one. keep_out_of_water already does exactly this shape for the other liquid that kills; lava only needs the same treatment, and unlike water there is no such thing as safely wading in.

rules.name: hunt_sheep_for_wool
rules.description: A bed is three wool and three planks, and the wool is the only part the bot cannot make: it has to walk to a sheep and let the hunting mode do the rest. Gated on owning no bed and less than three wool, so it stops the moment the bed is buildable rather than farming sheep forever.

rules.name: craft_a_bed
rules.description: Wool and wood in the bag: make the bed. This replaces the get_a_bed prompt, which paid for an LLM turn to look up a recipe that turned out to be the ordinary one -- three wool plus three planks, as !getCraftingPlan reports on this server. craft gathers the planks from logs itself. Runs at interrupt priority, not idle: with the wool and the wood in the bag and every gate satisfied, this sat unfired for five minutes while the goal loop talked -- only two rules fired at all in eight minutes, both of them interrupts:all. It is one shot, since owning or standing near a bed silences it, so it can interrupt exactly once and never again.

rules.name: place_the_bed
rules.description: A bed in the bag is worth nothing: it has to be on the ground before sleep_at_night can use it, and sleeping is what makes a night free. Placed only while sheltered, so the bed ends up in the hole or the base rather than in the open where the sleeping bot is a target. Runs at interrupt priority, not idle: with the wool and the wood in the bag and every gate satisfied, this sat unfired for five minutes while the goal loop talked -- only two rules fired at all in eight minutes, both of them interrupts:all. It is one shot, since owning or standing near a bed silences it, so it can interrupt exactly once and never again. And not where something is already hunting: the first bed this chain placed went down inside what the death telemetry showed to be a killing field, and sleep_at_night then walked back to it to be shot, five times in one game-day.

rules.name: eat_when_hungry
rules.description: One eating rule for the whole hunger band: at 14 hunger, eat, even mid-task. Replaces the old pair of eat_when_starving (7, interrupts all) and eat_before_hungry (17, idle-only) -- the idle gate meant a continuously busy bot ate nothing between comfortable and starving, which the agent noticed and wrote a self rule about. Gated on has_food so it never fires at an empty bag; consume clears its own trigger and the cooldown stops pantry chain-eating.

rules.name: take_food_from_storage
rules.description: Hungry with a chest in reach: restock from it. One withdraw per staple -- a withdraw for food you do not have is a cheap no-op, where asking the LLM which food is in the chest costs a full turn and it cannot see inside either. It deliberately does NOT eat: filling the bag makes has_food true, and eat_before_hungry/eat_when_starving take it from there on the next tick. Adding a consume here would make this an eating rule that fires with no food and re-triggers forever. Interrupts on purpose: the bot is already standing at the chest, so this is seconds of work, and going hungry next to full storage is the failure it exists to prevent. The is_idle gate came off with it: interrupt priority and an is_idle trigger cancel out, which is how the first pass at this audit left eight rules exactly as starved as before. Gated on having no food rather than on being idle: withdraw cannot lower hunger or move the chest, so with only those two triggers it would interrupt, achieve nothing, and interrupt again -- the validator caught exactly that.

rules.name: find_food_when_low
rules.description: Deep-emergency food prompt for when stayin_alive runs WITHOUT the food_gathering attribute layered on. With it, go_find_food_when_none_in_reach fires at 11 and almost always resolves the episode first, so this stays silent -- both prompts firing in one starvation episode is one paid turn too many.

do.message: You are running low on food and have nothing to eat. Get food NOW, before hunger starts costing health. In order of preference: !searchForBlock for carrots, potatoes or sweet_berry_bush and !collectBlocks them; !searchForEntity for a cow, pig, sheep or chicken and !attack it, then !smeltItem the raw meat if you have a furnace; or !goToRememberedPlace your base and !takeFromChest. Pick one and finish it.

rules.name: gather_wood_for_base
rules.description: Wood is tools, chests and shelter. Never be without a few logs.

rules.name: build_storage_chests
rules.description: Wood in the bag and nowhere to put anything. Craft and place; remembering where it is stays the reasoning loop's job, which it does from the behavior log without being asked. Interrupts on purpose: one shot, in place, and nothing can be banked until it exists. The is_idle gate came off with it: interrupt priority and an is_idle trigger cancel out, which is how the first pass at this audit left eight rules exactly as starved as before.

rules.name: expand_storage_room
rules.description: A base with chests and plenty of spare wood: add more. Same two named actions as building the first one.

rules.name: stow_bulk_at_base
rules.description: Dump the heavy junk in the chest so there is room for what matters. Interrupts on purpose: it only fires next to a chest with a full bag, so the walk is already paid for.

rules.name: stow_surplus_food
rules.description: Bank the extra food at the base, keeping a working stack on hand. Interrupts on purpose: it only fires next to a chest with a surplus, so the walk is already paid for.

rules.name: mine_stone_for_a_furnace
rules.description: The torch chain never fired once in soak 11 because it starts at a furnace and nothing ever built one. A furnace is eight cobblestone and cobblestone is one pickaxe swing away, so this is the missing first link, not a new ambition. Gated on already owning a pickaxe and on there being no furnace nearby, so it stops the moment the chain can proceed. Interrupts on purpose, the craft_a_pickaxe argument: rules are walked in list order and idleness goes to the first one that wants it, which is always gather_wood_for_base, so an idle gate this far down the list means never -- and the whole chain above it is blocked until this runs once. Eight blocks, a 300s cooldown, and the furnace it builds falsifies its own trigger for good.

rules.name: build_a_furnace
rules.description: Second link of the torch chain: cobblestone in the bag and no furnace at camp. One shot, in place, and smelt_logs_for_torch_fuel is blocked until it happens, so it interrupts rather than waiting for an idle moment that a bad night never gives.

rules.name: smelt_logs_for_torch_fuel
rules.description: Free half of the torch chain: charcoal from logs beats hunting coal ore (no stone pick, no paid search -- gather_wood_for_base already keeps logs coming). Gated on a furnace being near and torches actually being low, so it does not turn every furnace visit into a smelting session. Interrupts on purpose: it stands at the furnace and stops itself, and an idle gate this far down the rule list is a gate that never opens -- gather_wood_for_base takes every idle moment first.

rules.name: craft_torches
rules.description: Middle of the torch chain: fuel plus sticks becomes light. craft gathers intermediate sticks itself, so the only real gates are fuel on hand and torches low. dig_in already places a carried torch, and light_the_camp spends the rest. Interrupts on purpose: one craft, in place, and it is the only thing between charcoal and a lit camp. Idle this far down the list means never.

rules.name: light_the_camp
rules.description: Spawn-proof the respawn area: soak 8 lost 36 deaths to a mob camping the bed, and dark ground at camp is where bed-campers come from. Places ONE torch per fire, gated on no torch within 8, so coverage accumulates as the bot moves around camp instead of re-placing forever (the remember_here lesson). "Camp" was originally a bed within 16, but eleven soaks in there has never been a bed -- a chest or a furnace marks the place the bot actually keeps returning to, and those are the ground worth lighting. Interrupts on purpose: one block placed where it stands. Idle this far down the list means never, which is why the ground at camp was still dark eleven soaks in.
